title: Global Payment Processing for Indian Businesses: How It Works & Fees
summary: Learn how global payment processing works, including fees, FX conversion, payment delays, FIRA, INR settlement, and what Indian businesses should know before choosing a solution.
body_markdown:
## **How Much Does Global Payment Processing Cost?**


The headline transaction fee is only part of the picture. Depending on the payment route, the total cost can include a transaction fee, FX markup, fixed charge, sending-bank fee, intermediary-bank fee, or receiving-bank charge.


That is why comparing the total amount paid or received is more useful than comparing transaction fees alone.


### **Costs Included in an International Payment**


A simple way to look at the flow is:


The exchange rate determines how much one currency is worth when converted into another. An FX markup is an additional margin applied to the exchange rate. It is different from a transaction fee, so a provider can charge a transaction fee even when it does not add an FX markup.


There can be other costs too. Card payments may involve acquiring, network, interchange, and processing costs. Bank transfers can involve charges from the sending bank, intermediary banks, or the receiving bank.


So, when a provider advertises 0% FX markup, that does not mean the payment has no cost. It means the provider is not adding an FX margin to its stated exchange rate.


### **Example: How a 0.5% Transaction Fee Affects the Amount Received**


Suppose an Indian business receives USD 2,000 and the applicable exchange rate is ₹83.68 per USD.


Amount received


USD 2,000


Exchange rate


₹83.68/USD


Gross INR value


₹1,67,360


0.5% transaction fee


₹836.80


Amount after transaction fee


₹1,66,523.20


**Note:** This example is meant only to show how a transaction fee changes the final amount. The actual amount received may differ because the exchange rate, fees, payment route, settlement terms, and other charges may change.


## **Why Do Global Payments Fail or Get Delayed?**


International payments can get stuck for reasons unrelated to the amount being sent. Incorrect beneficiary details, an unsupported currency, a compliance review, or even a bank holiday can affect the payment.


### **Why Can a Global Payment Fail?**


Some of the more common reasons are:


-


**Incorrect payment details:** A wrong account number, IBAN, SWIFT/BIC code, routing detail, or beneficiary name can lead to rejection.


-


**Unsupported currency or route:** The bank or provider may not support the selected currency or payment path.


-


**Insufficient funds or limits:** The payer may not have enough funds, or the payment may exceed an applicable transaction limit.


-


**Missing information:** Incomplete or inconsistent details can prevent the transaction from being processed.


-


**Compliance checks:** AML, KYC, sanctions screening, or other checks may require additional information or stop the payment.


-


**Bank rejection:** One of the banks involved may reject the transaction because of its internal rules or the information provided.


-


**Technical problems:** A temporary issue with a bank, network, or payment provider can also interrupt processing.


### **Why Can a Global Payment Be Delayed?**


A payment can be valid and still take longer than expected. Common causes include:


-


**Bank cut-off times:** A payment submitted after the bank's cut-off may move to the next processing window.


-


**Weekends and holidays:** The sending and receiving countries may have different banking holidays or working schedules.


-


**Time-zone differences:** The payment may reach the next bank after its business hours have ended.


-


**Intermediary banks:** More institutions in the payment chain can mean more processing stages.


-


**Compliance reviews:** The bank or provider may pause the payment while checking the transaction or requesting documents.


-


**Routing issues:** A payment may need to move through another available route.


-


**Technical issues:** Temporary system problems can hold up an otherwise valid transaction.


If a payment is delayed, check its status before resending it. Confirm the beneficiary details, currency, and payment route, and respond to any request for additional information.


Do not resend a payment while it is still pending until you confirm its status. Otherwise, you could end up making the same payment twice.


## **What Does Global Payment Processing Mean for Indian Businesses?**


For an Indian business, receiving or sending money internationally involves more than simply getting the funds into a bank account.


Depending on the transaction, the business may need to deal with:


-


Payment purpose and transaction classification


-


Currency conversion


-


INR settlement


-


Invoices and supporting documents


-


Purpose codes


-


Remittance records


-


Applicable[FEMA and RBI requirements](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/how-infinityapp-follows-rbi-guidelines)


-


Export-related reporting or declarations, where applicable


According to[NITI Aayog](https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-06/Trade-Watch-Quarterly-Jan-March-Q4-FY26.pdf) , India’s total merchandise and services trade reached **$1.84 trillion in FY2025-26** . This reflects the scale of India’s trade with global markets and the growing need for businesses to manage cross-border payments efficiently.


The process differs for each transaction. Money received for an exported service, for example, may be subject to different requirements than an import payment, investment, loan, or other foreign-exchange transaction.


### **How Do RBI and FEMA Apply to International Payments?**


The **Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA)** provides the broader legal framework for foreign-exchange transactions in India, along with the regulations and directions issued under it.


Authorised Dealer (AD) banks handle eligible foreign-exchange transactions. Depending on the payment, they may also carry out checks, collect documents, handle reporting, and manage the applicable settlement process.


The exact requirements depend on what the payment represents. For instance, an Indian business receiving money from an overseas customer for an eligible service export may need to provide transaction details and supporting records so that the payment can be classified and settled correctly.


If you are unsure about the requirements for a particular transaction, confirm them with your Authorised Dealer bank or a qualified professional.


### **What Should Indian Service Exporters Know About the 2026 Export Framework?**


India updated its foreign-exchange framework for exports of goods and services in 2026. The applicable documentation and reporting requirements depend on the type of export, the transaction, and the current RBI framework.


An overseas payment is not automatically an export transaction that follows one standard[declaration](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/export-declaration-form) or reporting process. Service exporters should check the latest RBI requirements and confirm the applicable process with their Authorised Dealer bank before relying on a specific form, declaration, or deadline.


### **What are FIRA and Purpose Codes Used For?**


A purpose code tells the bank what a foreign-exchange transaction is for. It helps the bank classify the payment correctly.


[FIRA](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/what-is-fira-its-importance-for-freelancers-in-india) , or another applicable inward-remittance record, documents money received from overseas. The exact document and process can vary by bank and transaction.


## **How Should You Choose a Global Payment Processing Solution?**


The best place to start isn't the provider's fee page. Start with the way your business actually moves money.


A business receiving payments from overseas clients may need something quite different from a company running international e-commerce checkout or making supplier payouts.


Here are seven things worth checking:


1.


**Payment flow:** Are you receiving payments, sending them, or doing both?


2.


**Countries and currencies:** Does the provider support the markets and currencies you actually use?


3.


**Payment methods:** Can your customers or business use the required methods, such as cards, bank transfers, payment links, or local payment methods?


4.


**Total cost:** Look at transaction fees, exchange rates, FX markup, fixed charges, and bank or intermediary costs together.


5.


**Settlement:** Find out where the money settles, which currencies it supports, and when the funds become available.


6.


**Documentation and compliance:** Understand what KYC information, invoices, transaction details, remittance records, and other documents you may need.


7.


**Tracking and reconciliation:** Make sure you can see payment status and retrieve records that match invoices and accounting entries.


8.


**Fund flow and scalability:** Understand which banking and financial institutions are involved, whether the provider holds funds, and whether the setup can handle your expected transaction volume as the business grows.

## **Frequently Asked Questions About Global Payment Processing**


### **1. Why did I receive less money than the amount sent internationally?**


The amount you receive may be lower because of the exchange rate, FX markup, transaction fees, intermediary-bank charges, receiving-bank fees, or other applicable costs.


### **2. How long does an international payment take to reach India?**


There is no single processing time for every international payment. The timing can depend on the payment method, currency, banks involved, intermediary institutions, compliance checks, cut-off times, weekends, holidays, and the route used for the payment.


### **3. Can Indian freelancers receive payments from overseas clients?**


Yes. Indian freelancers can receive payments from overseas clients through supported international payment routes, subject to applicable foreign-exchange and transaction requirements.


Depending on the payment, they may need an invoice, payment purpose, purpose code, remittance details, or other supporting information.


### **4. Does 0% FX Markup mean international payments are free?**


No. It only means the provider does not add an FX margin to its stated exchange rate. Transaction fees, fixed charges, intermediary-bank fees, receiving-bank charges, and other costs can still apply.


### **5. What information does a business need to receive an international payment?**


The business will generally need its beneficiary or business details, relevant bank or account details, payment currency, and payment purpose. The bank or payment provider may also ask for an invoice, KYC information, or other supporting documents depending on the transaction.
